pr.title: Move condition enabling the pass to `is_enabled`
pr.description: The practical motivation is to omit the pass from -Zdump-mir=all when disabled.
pr.author: tmiasko

processing.reason: The PR only moves `sess.emit_lifetime_markers()` from a `run_pass` early return into `MirPass::is_enabled` for `RemoveStorageMarkers`. Both original and corrected gating produce identical MIR when lifetime markers are enabled: originally `is_enabled` returns true and `run_pass` immediately returns before retaining/filtering statements; after the patch `is_enabled` returns false so `run_pass` is skipped. The observable difference is only whether the disabled pass appears in `-Zdump-mir=all` pass membership, not any numeric/boolean/character value produced by compiled Rust code. Thus no source-grounded pair of ordinary Rust functions with identical signatures and inputs can yield different defined runtime values through this transformation; fabricating one would require an unrelated semantic rewrite, which the instructions forbid.

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `RemoveStorageMarkers::is_enabled` returned `sess.mir_opt_level() > 0`, while the lifetime-marker guard was inside `run_pass`: `if tcx.sess.emit_lifetime_markers() { return; }`. Therefore, when lifetime markers were requested, the pass was still considered enabled and still ran as a no-op, including appearing in `-Zdump-mir=all` output.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect placement of the disable condition in `run_pass` instead of `is_enabled` left the pass registered as enabled when `emit_lifetime_markers()` was true. The corrected transformation moves the condition into `is_enabled`: `sess.mir_opt_level() > 0 && !sess.emit_lifetime_markers()`. This changes pass gating and MIR-dump visibility, not the statement-retention rewrite itself.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust compiler sessions compiling a MIR body containing storage markers, parameterized by `sess.mir_opt_level()` and `sess.emit_lifetime_markers()`. A focused pair should differ only in whether the disable condition is checked in `run_pass` versus `is_enabled`; include a case with `mir_opt_level() > 0` and `emit_lifetime_markers()` true.
analysis.summary: Historical optimization PR moved the `emit_lifetime_markers()` disable condition from `RemoveStorageMarkers::run_pass` into `MirPass::is_enabled`, so a disabled pass is omitted from `-Zdump-mir=all`. This is a pass-gating/dump-visibility change, not a change to MIR semantics. No tests or compiler execution were provided in the patch.
analysis.trigger: Compiling with `mir_opt_level() > 0` while `emit_lifetime_markers()` is true, particularly when inspecting passes collected by `-Zdump-mir=all`.
preconditions: `RemoveStorageMarkers` is registered as a MIR pass.
MIR opt level is greater than zero.
MIR dump collection such as `-Zdump-mir=all` is used to observe pass membership.
pitfalls: Do not conflate pass membership in MIR dumps with the actual `StorageLive`/`StorageDead` retention transformation; moving the guard does not alter retained statements.
Do not expect `run_pass` to execute when `is_enabled` returns false.
The patch contains no regression test changes, so any test design must be inferred from the pass-gating change rather than from added test cases.
This is an optimization of dump visibility/pass gating, not a confirmed miscompilation bug fix.
analysis.testStrategy: Construct two compilations that differ only in the placement of the `emit_lifetime_markers()` guard: one with the guard in `run_pass`, one with it in `is_enabled`. Compile a MIR body containing storage markers with `mir_opt_level() > 0` and lifetime markers enabled, run with `-Zdump-mir=all`, and check that the disabled pass is absent from dump membership under the corrected gating while MIR output remains equivalent. Contrast with lifetime markers disabled, where the pass should be enabled and its storage-marker removal observable.
evidence: The practical motivation is to omit the pass from -Zdump-mir=all when disabled.
